            - link "Coroutines" [ref=f83e102] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../glossary.html#term-coroutine
            - text: "declared with the async/await syntax is the preferred way of writing asyncio applications. For example, the following snippet of code prints “hello”, waits 1 second, and then prints “world”:"
          - generic [ref=f83e103]: ">>> import asyncio >>> async def main(): ... print('hello') ... await asyncio.sleep(1) ... print('world') >>> asyncio.run(main()) hello world"
          - paragraph [ref=f83e106]: "Note that simply calling a coroutine will not schedule it to be executed:"
          - generic [ref=f83e107]: ">>> main() <coroutine object main at 0x1053bb7c8>"
          - paragraph [ref=f83e110]: "To actually run a coroutine, asyncio provides the following mechanisms:"
          - list [ref=f83e111]:
            - listitem [ref=f83e112]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e113]:
                - text: The
                - link [ref=f83e114] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-runner.html#asyncio.run
                  - code [ref=f83e115]: asyncio.run()
                - text: function to run the top-level entry point “main()” function (see the above example.)
            - listitem [ref=f83e116]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e117]:
                - text: Awaiting on a coroutine. The following snippet of code will print “hello” after waiting for 1 second, and then print “world” after waiting for
                - emphasis [ref=f83e118]: another
                - text: "2 seconds:"
              - generic [ref=f83e119]: "import asyncio import time async def say_after(delay, what): await asyncio.sleep(delay) print(what) async def main(): print(f\"started at {time.strftime('%X')}\") await say_after(1, 'hello') await say_after(2, 'world') print(f\"finished at {time.strftime('%X')}\") asyncio.run(main())"
              - paragraph [ref=f83e122]: "Expected output:"
              - generic [ref=f83e123]: started at 17:13:52 hello world finished at 17:13:55
            - listitem [ref=f83e126]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e127]:
                - text: The
                - link [ref=f83e128] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.create_task"
                  - code [ref=f83e129]: asyncio.create_task()
                - text: function to run coroutines concurrently as asyncio
                - link [ref=f83e130] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.Task"
                  - code [ref=f83e131]: Tasks
                - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f83e132]:
                - text: Let’s modify the above example and run two
                - code [ref=f83e133]: say_after
                - text: coroutines
                - emphasis [ref=f83e134]: concurrently
                - text: ":"
              - generic [ref=f83e135]: "async def main(): task1 = asyncio.create_task( say_after(1, 'hello')) task2 = asyncio.create_task( say_after(2, 'world')) print(f\"started at {time.strftime('%X')}\") # Wait until both tasks are completed (should take # around 2 seconds.) await task1 await task2 print(f\"finished at {time.strftime('%X')}\")"
              - paragraph [ref=f83e138]: "Note that expected output now shows that the snippet runs 1 second faster than before:"
              - generic [ref=f83e139]: started at 17:14:32 hello world finished at 17:14:34
            - listitem [ref=f83e142]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e143]:
                - text: The
                - link [ref=f83e144] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.TaskGroup"
                  - code [ref=f83e145]: asyncio.TaskGroup
                - text: class provides a more modern alternative to
                - link [ref=f83e146] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.create_task"
                  - code [ref=f83e147]: create_task()
                - text: ". Using this API, the last example becomes:"
              - generic [ref=f83e148]: "async def main(): async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: task1 = tg.create_task( say_after(1, 'hello')) task2 = tg.create_task( say_after(2, 'world')) print(f\"started at {time.strftime('%X')}\") # The await is implicit when the context manager exits. print(f\"finished at {time.strftime('%X')}\")"
              - paragraph [ref=f83e151]: The timing and output should be the same as for the previous version.

        - generic [ref=f83e156]:
          - heading [level=2] [ref=f83e157]:
            - link "Awaitables" [ref=f83e158] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#id3"
          - paragraph [ref=f83e159]:
            - text: We say that an object is an
            - strong [ref=f83e160]: awaitable
            - text: object if it can be used in an
            - link [ref=f83e161] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../reference/expressions.html#await
              - code [ref=f83e162]: await
            - text: expression. Many asyncio APIs are designed to accept awaitables.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e163]:
            - text: There are three main types of
            - emphasis [ref=f83e164]: awaitable
            - text: "objects:"
            - strong [ref=f83e165]: coroutines
            - text: ","
            - strong [ref=f83e166]: Tasks
            - text: ", and"
            - strong [ref=f83e167]: Futures
            - text: .
          - paragraph [ref=f83e168]: Coroutines
          - paragraph [ref=f83e169]:
            - text: Python coroutines are
            - emphasis [ref=f83e170]: awaitables
            - text: "and therefore can be awaited from other coroutines:"
          - generic [ref=f83e171]: "import asyncio async def nested(): return 42 async def main(): # Nothing happens if we just call \"nested()\". # A coroutine object is created but not awaited, # so it *won't run at all*. nested() # will raise a \"RuntimeWarning\". # Let's do it differently now and await it: print(await nested()) # will print \"42\". asyncio.run(main())"
          - generic [ref=f83e174]:
            - paragraph [ref=f83e175]: "Important:"
            - paragraph [ref=f83e176]: "In this documentation the term “coroutine” can be used for two closely related concepts:"
            - list [ref=f83e177]:
              - listitem [ref=f83e178]:
                - paragraph [ref=f83e179]:
                  - text: a
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e180]: coroutine function
                  - text: ": an"
                  - link [ref=f83e181] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: ../reference/compound_stmts.html#async-def
                    - code [ref=f83e182]: async def
                  - text: function;
              - listitem [ref=f83e183]:
                - paragraph [ref=f83e184]:
                  - text: a
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e185]: coroutine object
                  - text: ": an object returned by calling a"
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e186]: coroutine function
                  - text: .
          - paragraph [ref=f83e187]: Tasks
          - paragraph [ref=f83e188]:
            - emphasis [ref=f83e189]: Tasks
            - text: are used to schedule coroutines
            - emphasis [ref=f83e190]: concurrently
            - text: .
          - paragraph [ref=f83e191]:
            - text: When a coroutine is wrapped into a
            - emphasis [ref=f83e192]: Task
            - text: with functions like
            - link [ref=f83e193] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#asyncio.create_task"
              - code [ref=f83e194]: asyncio.create_task()
            - text: "the coroutine is automatically scheduled to run soon:"
          - generic [ref=f83e195]: "import asyncio async def nested(): return 42 async def main(): # Schedule nested() to run soon concurrently # with \"main()\". task = asyncio.create_task(nested()) # \"task\" can now be used to cancel \"nested()\", or # can simply be awaited to wait until it is complete: await task asyncio.run(main())"
          - paragraph [ref=f83e198]: Futures
          - paragraph [ref=f83e199]:
            - text: A
            - link [ref=f83e200] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: asyncio-future.html#asyncio.Future
              - code [ref=f83e201]: Future
            - text: is a special
            - strong [ref=f83e202]: low-level
            - text: awaitable object that represents an
            - strong [ref=f83e203]: eventual result
            - text: of an asynchronous operation.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e204]:
            - text: When a Future object is
            - emphasis [ref=f83e205]: awaited
            - text: it means that the coroutine will wait until the Future is resolved in some other place.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e206]: Future objects in asyncio are needed to allow callback-based code to be used with async/await.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e207]:
            - text: Normally
            - strong [ref=f83e208]: there is no need
            - text: to create Future objects at the application level code.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e209]: "Future objects, sometimes exposed by libraries and some asyncio APIs, can be awaited:"
          - generic [ref=f83e210]: "async def main(): await function_that_returns_a_future_object() # this is also valid: await asyncio.gather( function_that_returns_a_future_object(), some_python_coroutine() )"
          - paragraph [ref=f83e213]:
            - text: A good example of a low-level function that returns a Future object is
            - link [ref=f83e214] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: asyncio-eventloop.html#asyncio.loop.run_in_executor
              - code [ref=f83e215]: loop.run_in_executor()
            - text: .

          - heading [level=2] [ref=f83e217]:
            - link "Creating tasks" [ref=f83e218] [cursor=pointer]:

          - separator [ref=f83e222]
          - generic [ref=f83e223]:
            - term [ref=f83e224]:
              - generic [ref=f83e225]: asyncio.
              - generic [ref=f83e226]: create_task
              - text: (
              - emphasis [ref=f83e227]:
                - generic [ref=f83e228]: coro
              - text: ","
              - emphasis [ref=f83e229]:
                - generic "Keyword-only parameters separator (PEP 3102)" [ref=f83e231]: "*"
              - text: ","
              - emphasis [ref=f83e232]:
                - generic [ref=f83e233]: name
                - generic [ref=f83e234]: =

              - emphasis [ref=f83e236]:

                - generic [ref=f83e238]: =
                - generic [ref=f83e239]: None

              - emphasis [ref=f83e240]:
                - generic [ref=f83e241]: eager_start

                - generic [ref=f83e243]: None
              - text: ","
              - emphasis [ref=f83e244]:
                - generic [ref=f83e245]: "**"
                - generic [ref=f83e246]: kwargs
              - text: )
            - definition [ref=f83e247]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e248]:
                - text: Wrap the
                - emphasis [ref=f83e249]: coro
                - link "coroutine" [ref=f83e250] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#coroutine"
                - text: into a
                - link [ref=f83e251] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.Task"
                  - code [ref=f83e252]: Task
                - text: and schedule its execution. Return the Task object.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e253]:
                - text: The full function signature is largely the same as that of the
                - link [ref=f83e254] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.Task"
                  - code [ref=f83e255]: Task
                - text: constructor (or factory) - all of the keyword arguments to this function are passed through to that interface.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e256]:
                - text: An optional keyword-only
                - emphasis [ref=f83e257]: context
                - text: argument allows specifying a custom
                - link [ref=f83e258] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: contextvars.html#contextvars.Context
                  - code [ref=f83e259]: contextvars.Context
                - text: for the
                - emphasis [ref=f83e260]: coro
                - text: to run in. The current context copy is created when no
                - emphasis [ref=f83e261]: context
                - text: is provided.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e262]:
                - text: An optional keyword-only
                - emphasis [ref=f83e263]: eager_start
                - text: argument allows specifying if the task should execute eagerly during the call to create_task, or be scheduled later. If
                - emphasis [ref=f83e264]: eager_start
                - text: is not passed the mode set by
                - link [ref=f83e265] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-eventloop.html#asyncio.loop.set_task_factory
                  - code [ref=f83e266]: loop.set_task_factory()
                - text: will be used.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e267]:
                - text: The task is executed in the loop returned by
                - link [ref=f83e268] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-eventloop.html#asyncio.get_running_loop
                  - code [ref=f83e269]: get_running_loop()
                - text: ","
                - link [ref=f83e270] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError
                  - code [ref=f83e271]: RuntimeError
                - text: is raised if there is no running loop in current thread.
              - generic [ref=f83e272]:
                - paragraph [ref=f83e273]: "Note:"
                - paragraph [ref=f83e274]:
                  - link [ref=f83e275] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#asyncio.TaskGroup.create_task"
                    - code [ref=f83e276]: asyncio.TaskGroup.create_task()
                  - text: is a new alternative leveraging structural concurrency; it allows for waiting for a group of related tasks with strong safety guarantees.
              - generic [ref=f83e277]:
                - paragraph [ref=f83e278]: "Important:"
                - paragraph [ref=f83e279]: "Save a reference to the result of this function, to avoid a task disappearing mid-execution. The event loop only keeps weak references to tasks. A task that isn’t referenced elsewhere may get garbage collected at any time, even before it’s done. For reliable “fire-and-forget” background tasks, gather them in a collection:"
                - generic [ref=f83e280]: "background_tasks = set() for i in range(10): task = asyncio.create_task(some_coro(param=i)) # Add task to the set. This creates a strong reference. background_tasks.add(task) # To prevent keeping references to finished tasks forever, # make each task remove its own reference from the set after # completion: task.add_done_callback(background_tasks.discard)"
                - paragraph [ref=f83e283]:
                  - text: Note that this approach never awaits the tasks, so if a task fails, its exception is never retrieved and asyncio logs a “Task exception was never retrieved” message when the task is garbage collected. To avoid this, use
                  - link [ref=f83e284] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#asyncio.TaskGroup"
                    - code [ref=f83e285]: asyncio.TaskGroup
                  - text: "which keeps a strong reference to each task, awaits them and propagates their exceptions:"
                - generic [ref=f83e286]: "async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: for i in range(10): tg.create_task(some_coro(param=i))"
              - paragraph [ref=f83e290]: Added in version 3.7.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e292]:
                - text: "Changed in version 3.8: Added the"
                - emphasis [ref=f83e293]: name
                - text: parameter.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e295]:
                - text: "Changed in version 3.11: Added the"
                - emphasis [ref=f83e296]: context
                - text: parameter.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e298]:
                - text: "Changed in version 3.14: Added the"
                - emphasis [ref=f83e299]: eager_start
                - text: parameter by passing on all
                - emphasis [ref=f83e300]: kwargs
                - text: .
        - generic [ref=f83e301]:
          - heading [level=2] [ref=f83e302]:
            - link "Task cancellation" [ref=f83e303] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#id5"
          - paragraph [ref=f83e304]:
            - text: Tasks can easily and safely be cancelled. When a task is cancelled,
            - link [ref=f83e305] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
              - code [ref=f83e306]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: will be raised in the task at the next opportunity.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e307]:
            - text: It is recommended that coroutines use
            - code [ref=f83e308]: try/finally
            - text: blocks to robustly perform clean-up logic. In case
            - link [ref=f83e309] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
              - code [ref=f83e310]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: is explicitly caught, it should generally be propagated when clean-up is complete.
            - code [ref=f83e311]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: directly subclasses
            - link [ref=f83e312] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#BaseException
              - code [ref=f83e313]: BaseException
            - text: so most code will not need to be aware of it.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e314]:
            - text: The asyncio components that enable structured concurrency, like
            - link [ref=f83e315] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#asyncio.TaskGroup"
              - code [ref=f83e316]: asyncio.TaskGroup
            - text: and
            - link [ref=f83e317] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#asyncio.timeout"
              - code [ref=f83e318]: asyncio.timeout()
            - text: ", are implemented using cancellation internally and might misbehave if a coroutine swallows"
            - link [ref=f83e319] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
              - code [ref=f83e320]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: . Similarly, user code should not generally call
            - link [ref=f83e321] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#asyncio.Task.uncancel"
              - code [ref=f83e322]: uncancel
            - text: . However, in cases when suppressing
            - code [ref=f83e323]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: is truly desired, it is necessary to also call
            - code [ref=f83e324]: uncancel()
            - text: to completely remove the cancellation state.
        - generic [ref=f83e325]:
          - heading [level=2] [ref=f83e326]:
            - link "Task groups" [ref=f83e327] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#id6"
          - paragraph [ref=f83e328]: Task groups combine a task creation API with a convenient and reliable way to wait for all tasks in the group to finish.
          - generic [ref=f83e329]:
            - term [ref=f83e330]:
              - emphasis [ref=f83e331]:
                - generic [ref=f83e332]: class
              - generic [ref=f83e333]: asyncio.
              - generic [ref=f83e334]: TaskGroup
            - definition [ref=f83e335]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e336]:
                - text: An
                - link "asynchronous context manager" [ref=f83e337] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: ../reference/datamodel.html#async-context-managers
                - text: holding a group of tasks. Tasks can be added to the group using
                - link [ref=f83e338] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.create_task"
                  - code [ref=f83e339]: create_task()
                - text: . All tasks are awaited when the context manager exits.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e341]: Added in version 3.11.
              - generic [ref=f83e342]:
                - term [ref=f83e343]:
                  - generic [ref=f83e344]: create_task
                  - text: (
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e345]:
                    - generic [ref=f83e346]: coro
                  - text: ","
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e347]:
                    - generic "Keyword-only parameters separator (PEP 3102)" [ref=f83e349]: "*"
                  - text: ","
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e350]:
                    - generic [ref=f83e351]: name
                    - generic [ref=f83e352]: =
                    - generic [ref=f83e353]: None
                  - text: ","
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e354]:
                    - generic [ref=f83e355]: context
                    - generic [ref=f83e356]: =
                    - generic [ref=f83e357]: None
                  - text: ","
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e358]:
                    - generic [ref=f83e359]: eager_start
                    - generic [ref=f83e360]: =
                    - generic [ref=f83e361]: None
                  - text: ","
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e362]:
                    - generic [ref=f83e363]: "**"
                    - generic [ref=f83e364]: kwargs
                  - text: )
                - definition [ref=f83e365]:
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e366]:
                    - text: Create a task in this task group. The signature matches that of
                    - link [ref=f83e367] [cursor=pointer]:
                      - /url: "#asyncio.create_task"
                      - code [ref=f83e368]: asyncio.create_task()
                    - text: . If the task group is inactive (e.g. not yet entered, already finished, or in the process of shutting down), we will close the given
                    - code [ref=f83e369]: coro
                    - text: and raise
                    - link [ref=f83e370] [cursor=pointer]:

                      - code [ref=f83e371]: RuntimeError
                    - text: .
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e373]: "Changed in version 3.13: Close the given coroutine if the task group is not active."
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e375]:

                    - emphasis [ref=f83e376]: kwargs
                    - text: to
                    - link [ref=f83e377] [cursor=pointer]:

                      - code [ref=f83e378]: loop.create_task()
              - generic [ref=f83e379]:
                - term [ref=f83e380]:
                  - generic [ref=f83e381]: cancel
                  - text: ()
                - definition [ref=f83e382]:
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e383]: Cancel the task group. This is a non-exceptional, early exit of the task group’s lifetime – useful once the group’s goal has been met or its services no longer needed.
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e384]:
                    - link [ref=f83e385] [cursor=pointer]:
                      - /url: "#asyncio.Task.cancel"
                      - code [ref=f83e386]: cancel()
                    - text: will be called on any tasks in the group that aren’t yet done, as well as the parent (body) of the group. The task group context manager will exit
                    - emphasis [ref=f83e387]: without
                    - link [ref=f83e388] [cursor=pointer]:
                      - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
                      - code [ref=f83e389]: asyncio.CancelledError
                    - text: being raised.
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e390]:
                    - text: If
                    - code [ref=f83e391]: cancel()
                    - text: is called before entering the task group, the group will be cancelled upon entry. This is useful for patterns where one piece of code passes an unused
                    - link [ref=f83e392] [cursor=pointer]:
                      - /url: "#asyncio.TaskGroup"
                      - code [ref=f83e393]: asyncio.TaskGroup
                    - text: instance to another in order to have the ability to cancel anything run within the group.
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e394]:
                    - code [ref=f83e395]: cancel()
                    - text: is idempotent and may be called after the task group has already exited.
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e396]:
                    - text: Some ways to use
                    - code [ref=f83e397]: cancel()
                    - text: ":"
                  - list [ref=f83e398]:
                    - listitem [ref=f83e399]:
                      - paragraph [ref=f83e400]: call it from the task group body based on some condition or event
                    - listitem [ref=f83e401]:
                      - paragraph [ref=f83e402]:
                        - text: pass the task group instance to child tasks via
                        - link [ref=f83e403] [cursor=pointer]:
                          - /url: "#asyncio.create_task"
                          - code [ref=f83e404]: create_task()
                        - text: ", allowing a child task to conditionally cancel the entire group"
                    - listitem [ref=f83e405]:
                      - paragraph [ref=f83e406]:
                        - text: pass the task group instance or bound
                        - code [ref=f83e407]: cancel()
                        - text: method to some other task
                        - emphasis [ref=f83e408]: before
                        - text: opening the task group, allowing remote cancellation
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e410]: Added in version 3.15.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e411]: "Example:"
          - generic [ref=f83e412]: "async def main(): async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: task1 = tg.create_task(some_coro(...)) task2 = tg.create_task(another_coro(...)) print(f\"Both tasks have completed now: {task1.result()}, {task2.result()}\")"
          - paragraph [ref=f83e415]:
            - text: The
            - code [ref=f83e416]: async with
            - text: statement will wait for all tasks in the group to finish. While waiting, new tasks may still be added to the group (for example, by passing
            - code [ref=f83e417]: tg
            - text: into one of the coroutines and calling
            - code [ref=f83e418]: tg.create_task()
            - text: in that coroutine). There is also opportunity to request termination of the entire task group with
            - code [ref=f83e419]: tg.cancel()
            - text: ", based on some condition. Once the last task has finished and the"
            - code [ref=f83e420]: async with
            - text: block is exited, no new tasks may be added to the group.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e421]:
            - text: The first time any of the tasks belonging to the group fails with an exception other than
            - link [ref=f83e422] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
              - code [ref=f83e423]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: ", the remaining tasks in the group are cancelled. No further tasks can then be added to the group. At this point, if the body of the"
            - code [ref=f83e424]: async with
            - text: statement is still active (i.e.,
            - link [ref=f83e425] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../reference/datamodel.html#object.__aexit__
              - code [ref=f83e426]: __aexit__()
            - text: hasn’t been called yet), the task directly containing the
            - code [ref=f83e427]: async with
            - text: statement is also cancelled. The resulting
            - code [ref=f83e428]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: will interrupt an
            - code [ref=f83e429]: await
            - text: ", but it will not bubble out of the containing"
            - code [ref=f83e430]: async with
            - text: statement.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e431]:
            - text: Once all tasks have finished, if any tasks have failed with an exception other than
            - link [ref=f83e432] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
              - code [ref=f83e433]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: ", those exceptions are combined in an"
            - link [ref=f83e434] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#ExceptionGroup
              - code [ref=f83e435]: ExceptionGroup
            - text: or
            - link [ref=f83e436] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#BaseExceptionGroup
              - code [ref=f83e437]: BaseExceptionGroup
            - text: (as appropriate; see their documentation) which is then raised.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e438]:
            - text: "Two base exceptions are treated specially: If any task fails with"
            - link [ref=f83e439] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#KeyboardInterrupt
              - code [ref=f83e440]: KeyboardInterrupt
            - text: or
            - link [ref=f83e441] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#SystemExit
              - code [ref=f83e442]: SystemExit
            - text: ", the task group still cancels the remaining tasks and waits for them, but then the initial"
            - code [ref=f83e443]: KeyboardInterrupt
            - text: or
            - code [ref=f83e444]: SystemExit
            - text: is re-raised instead of
            - link [ref=f83e445] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#ExceptionGroup
              - code [ref=f83e446]: ExceptionGroup
            - text: or
            - link [ref=f83e447] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#BaseExceptionGroup
              - code [ref=f83e448]: BaseExceptionGroup
            - text: .
          - paragraph [ref=f83e449]:
            - text: If the body of the
            - code [ref=f83e450]: async with
            - text: statement exits with an exception (so
            - link [ref=f83e451] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../reference/datamodel.html#object.__aexit__
              - code [ref=f83e452]: __aexit__()
            - text: "is called with an exception set), this is treated the same as if one of the tasks failed: the remaining tasks are cancelled and then waited for, and non-cancellation exceptions are grouped into an exception group and raised. The exception passed into"
            - code [ref=f83e453]: __aexit__()
            - text: ", unless it is"
            - link [ref=f83e454] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
              - code [ref=f83e455]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: ", is also included in the exception group. The same special case is made for"
            - link [ref=f83e456] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#KeyboardInterrupt
              - code [ref=f83e457]: KeyboardInterrupt
            - text: and
            - link [ref=f83e458] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#SystemExit
              - code [ref=f83e459]: SystemExit
            - text: as in the previous paragraph. There is an additional special case made only for the body of the
            - code [ref=f83e460]: async with
            - text: ": if it raises"
            - link [ref=f83e461] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#GeneratorExit
              - code [ref=f83e462]: GeneratorExit
            - text: and none of the other tasks raise exceptions that would be reported, then the
            - code [ref=f83e463]: GeneratorExit
            - text: is reraised.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e464]:
            - text: Task groups are careful not to mix up the internal cancellation used to “wake up” their
            - link [ref=f83e465] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../reference/datamodel.html#object.__aexit__
              - code [ref=f83e466]: __aexit__()
            - text: with cancellation requests for the task in which they are running made by other parties. In particular, when one task group is syntactically nested in another, and both experience an exception in one of their child tasks simultaneously, the inner task group will process its exceptions, and then the outer task group will receive another cancellation and process its own exceptions.
          - paragraph [ref=f83e467]:
            - text: In the case where a task group is cancelled externally and also must raise an
            - link [ref=f83e468] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#ExceptionGroup
              - code [ref=f83e469]: ExceptionGroup
            - text: ", it will call the parent task’s"
            - link [ref=f83e470] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#asyncio.Task.cancel"
              - code [ref=f83e471]: cancel()
            - text: method. This ensures that a
            - link [ref=f83e472] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
              - code [ref=f83e473]: asyncio.CancelledError
            - text: will be raised at the next
            - link [ref=f83e474] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../reference/expressions.html#await
              - code [ref=f83e475]: await
            - text: ", so the cancellation is not lost."
          - paragraph [ref=f83e476]:
            - text: Task groups preserve the cancellation count reported by
            - link [ref=f83e477] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#asyncio.Task.cancelling"
              - code [ref=f83e478]: asyncio.Task.cancelling()
            - text: .
          - paragraph [ref=f83e480]: "Changed in version 3.13: Improved handling of simultaneous internal and external cancellations and correct preservation of cancellation counts."
          - paragraph [ref=f83e482]:
            - text: "Changed in version 3.15: Addition of the special case for"
            - link [ref=f83e483] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: ../builtins/exceptions.html#GeneratorExit
              - code [ref=f83e484]: GeneratorExit
            - text: .
        - generic [ref=f83e485]:
          - heading [level=2] [ref=f83e486]:
            - link "Sleeping" [ref=f83e487] [cursor=pointer]:

              - paragraph [ref=f83e501]:

                - text: seconds.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e503]:
                - text: If
                - emphasis [ref=f83e504]: result
                - text: is provided, it is returned to the caller when the coroutine completes.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e505]:
                - code [ref=f83e506]: sleep()
                - text: always suspends the current task, allowing other tasks to run.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e507]: Setting the delay to 0 provides an optimized path to allow other tasks to run. This can be used by long-running functions to avoid blocking the event loop for the full duration of the function call.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e508]: "Example of coroutine displaying the current date every second for 5 seconds:"
              - generic [ref=f83e509]: "import asyncio import datetime as dt async def display_date(): loop = asyncio.get_running_loop() end_time = loop.time() + 5.0 while True: print(dt.datetime.now()) if (loop.time() + 1.0) >= end_time: break await asyncio.sleep(1) asyncio.run(display_date())"

        - generic [ref=f83e522]:
          - heading [level=2] [ref=f83e523]:
            - link "Running tasks concurrently" [ref=f83e524] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#id8"
          - generic [ref=f83e525]:
            - term [ref=f83e526]:
              - emphasis [ref=f83e527]: awaitable
              - generic [ref=f83e528]: asyncio.
              - generic [ref=f83e529]: gather
              - text: (
              - emphasis [ref=f83e530]:
                - generic [ref=f83e531]: "*"
                - generic [ref=f83e532]: aws
              - text: ","
              - emphasis [ref=f83e533]:
                - generic [ref=f83e534]: return_exceptions
                - generic [ref=f83e535]: =
                - generic [ref=f83e536]: "False"
              - text: )
            - definition [ref=f83e537]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e538]:
                - text: Run
                - link "awaitable objects" [ref=f83e539] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio-awaitables"
                - text: in the
                - emphasis [ref=f83e540]: aws
                - text: sequence
                - emphasis [ref=f83e541]: concurrently
                - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f83e542]:
                - text: If any awaitable in
                - emphasis [ref=f83e543]: aws
                - text: is a coroutine, it is automatically scheduled as a Task.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e544]:
                - text: If all awaitables are completed successfully, the result is an aggregate list of returned values. The order of result values corresponds to the order of awaitables in
                - emphasis [ref=f83e545]: aws
                - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f83e546]:
                - text: If
                - emphasis [ref=f83e547]: return_exceptions
                - text: is
                - code [ref=f83e548]: "False"
                - text: (default), the first raised exception is immediately propagated to the task that awaits on
                - code [ref=f83e549]: gather()
                - text: . Other awaitables in the
                - emphasis [ref=f83e550]: aws
                - text: sequence
                - strong [ref=f83e551]: won’t be cancelled
                - text: and will continue to run.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e552]:
                - text: If
                - emphasis [ref=f83e553]: return_exceptions
                - text: is
                - code [ref=f83e554]: "True"
                - text: ", exceptions are treated the same as successful results, and aggregated in the result list."
              - paragraph [ref=f83e555]:
                - text: If
                - code [ref=f83e556]: gather()
                - text: is
                - emphasis [ref=f83e557]: cancelled
                - text: ", all submitted awaitables (that have not completed yet) are also"
                - emphasis [ref=f83e558]: cancelled
                - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f83e559]:
                - text: If any Task or Future from the
                - emphasis [ref=f83e560]: aws
                - text: sequence is
                - emphasis [ref=f83e561]: cancelled
                - text: ", it is treated as if it raised"
                - link [ref=f83e562] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
                  - code [ref=f83e563]: CancelledError
                - text: – the
                - code [ref=f83e564]: gather()
                - text: call is
                - strong [ref=f83e565]: not
                - text: cancelled in this case. This is to prevent the cancellation of one submitted Task/Future to cause other Tasks/Futures to be cancelled.
              - generic [ref=f83e566]:
                - paragraph [ref=f83e567]: "Note:"
                - paragraph [ref=f83e568]:
                  - text: A new alternative to create and run tasks concurrently and wait for their completion is
                  - link [ref=f83e569] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#asyncio.TaskGroup"
                    - code [ref=f83e570]: asyncio.TaskGroup
                  - text: .
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e571]: TaskGroup
                  - text: provides stronger safety guarantees than
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e572]: gather
                  - text: "for scheduling a nesting of subtasks: if a task (or a subtask, a task scheduled by a task) raises an exception,"
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e573]: TaskGroup
                  - text: will, while
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e574]: gather
                  - text: will not, cancel the remaining scheduled tasks.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e575]: "Example:"
              - generic [ref=f83e576]: "import asyncio async def factorial(name, number): f = 1 for i in range(2, number + 1): print(f\"Task {name}: Compute factorial({number}), currently i={i}...\") await asyncio.sleep(1) f *= i print(f\"Task {name}: factorial({number}) = {f}\") return f async def main(): # Schedule three calls *concurrently*: L = await asyncio.gather( factorial(\"A\", 2), factorial(\"B\", 3), factorial(\"C\", 4), ) print(L) asyncio.run(main()) # Expected output: # # Task A: Compute factorial(2), currently i=2... # Task B: Compute factorial(3), currently i=2... # Task C: Compute factorial(4), currently i=2... # Task A: factorial(2) = 2 # Task B: Compute factorial(3), currently i=3... # Task C: Compute factorial(4), currently i=3... # Task B: factorial(3) = 6 # Task C: Compute factorial(4), currently i=4... # Task C: factorial(4) = 24 # [2, 6, 24]"
              - generic [ref=f83e579]:
                - paragraph [ref=f83e580]: "Note:"
                - paragraph [ref=f83e581]:
                  - text: If
                  - emphasis [ref=f83e582]: return_exceptions
                  - text: is false, cancelling gather() after it has been marked done won’t cancel any submitted awaitables. For instance, gather can be marked done after propagating an exception to the caller, therefore, calling
                  - code [ref=f83e583]: gather.cancel()
                  - text: after catching an exception (raised by one of the awaitables) from gather won’t cancel any other awaitables.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e585]:
                - text: "Changed in version 3.7: If the"
                - emphasis [ref=f83e586]: gather
                - text: itself is cancelled, the cancellation is propagated regardless of
                - emphasis [ref=f83e587]: return_exceptions
                - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f83e589]:
                - text: "Changed in version 3.10: Removed the"
                - emphasis [ref=f83e590]: loop
                - text: parameter.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e592]: "Deprecated since version 3.10: Deprecation warning is emitted if no positional arguments are provided or not all positional arguments are Future-like objects and there is no running event loop."
        - generic [ref=f83e593]:
          - heading [level=2] [ref=f83e594]:
            - link "Eager task factory" [ref=f83e595] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#id9"
          - generic [ref=f83e596]:
            - term [ref=f83e597]:
              - generic [ref=f83e598]: asyncio.
              - generic [ref=f83e599]: eager_task_factory
              - text: (
              - emphasis [ref=f83e600]:
                - generic [ref=f83e601]: loop
              - text: ","
              - emphasis [ref=f83e602]:
                - generic [ref=f83e603]: coro
              - text: ","
              - emphasis [ref=f83e604]:
                - generic "Keyword-only parameters separator (PEP 3102)" [ref=f83e606]: "*"
              - text: ","
              - emphasis [ref=f83e607]:
                - generic [ref=f83e608]: name
                - generic [ref=f83e609]: =
                - generic [ref=f83e610]: None
              - text: ","
              - emphasis [ref=f83e611]:
                - generic [ref=f83e612]: context
                - generic [ref=f83e613]: =
                - generic [ref=f83e614]: None
              - text: )
            - definition [ref=f83e615]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e616]: A task factory for eager task execution.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e617]:
                - text: When using this factory (via
                - link [ref=f83e618] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-eventloop.html#asyncio.loop.set_task_factory
                  - code [ref=f83e619]: loop.set_task_factory(asyncio.eager_task_factory)
                - text: ), coroutines begin execution synchronously during
                - link [ref=f83e620] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.Task"
                  - code [ref=f83e621]: Task
                - text: construction. Tasks are only scheduled on the event loop if they block. This can be a performance improvement as the overhead of loop scheduling is avoided for coroutines that complete synchronously.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e622]: A common example where this is beneficial is coroutines which employ caching or memoization to avoid actual I/O when possible.
              - generic [ref=f83e623]:
                - paragraph [ref=f83e624]: "Note:"
                - paragraph [ref=f83e625]: Immediate execution of the coroutine is a semantic change. If the coroutine returns or raises, the task is never scheduled to the event loop. If the coroutine execution blocks, the task is scheduled to the event loop. This change may introduce behavior changes to existing applications. For example, the application’s task execution order is likely to change.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e627]: Added in version 3.12.

                        - definition

              - paragraph [ref=f83e976]:

                  - /url: "#asyncio.wait_for"
                  - code [ref=f83e978]: wait_for()
                - text: ","

                - code [ref=f83e981]: wait()
                - text: is cancelled, the futures in
                - emphasis [ref=f83e982]: aws
                - text: are not cancelled and continue to run.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e984]:

                - text: in the
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1007]: aws
                - text: iterable concurrently. The returned object can be iterated to obtain the results of the awaitables as they finish.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1008]:

                - text: can be iterated as an
                - link "asynchronous iterator" [ref=f83e1010] [cursor=pointer]:

                - link "iterator" [ref=f83e1011] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: ../glossary.html#term-iterator
                - text: ". When asynchronous iteration is used, the originally-supplied awaitables are yielded if they are tasks or futures. This makes it easy to correlate previously-scheduled tasks with their results. Example:"
              - generic [ref=f83e1012]: "ipv4_connect = create_task(open_connection(\"127.0.0.1\", 80)) ipv6_connect = create_task(open_connection(\"::1\", 80)) tasks = [ipv4_connect, ipv6_connect] async for earliest_connect in as_completed(tasks): # earliest_connect is done.               - paragraph [ref=f83e1015]: During asynchronous iteration, implicitly-created tasks will be yielded for supplied awaitables that aren’t tasks or futures.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1016]: "When used as a plain iterator, each iteration yields a new coroutine that returns the result or raises the exception of the next completed awaitable. This pattern is compatible with Python versions older than 3.13:"
              - generic [ref=f83e1017]: "ipv4_connect = create_task(open_connection(\"127.0.0.1\", 80)) ipv6_connect = create_task(open_connection(\"::1\", 80)) tasks = [ipv4_connect, ipv6_connect] for next_connect in as_completed(tasks): # next_connect is not one of the original task objects.               - paragraph [ref=f83e1020]:

                - text: is raised if the timeout occurs before all awaitables are done. This is raised by the
                - code [ref=f83e1023]: async for

              - paragraph [ref=f83e1024]:

            - definition [ref=f83e1058]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1059]:
                - text: Asynchronously run function
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1060]: func
                - text: in a separate thread.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1061]:
                - text: Any *args and **kwargs supplied for this function are directly passed to
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1062]: func
                - text: . Also, the current
                - link [ref=f83e1063] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: contextvars.html#contextvars.Context
                  - code [ref=f83e1064]: contextvars.Context
                - text: is propagated, allowing context variables from the event loop thread to be accessed in the separate thread.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1065]:
                - text: Return a coroutine that can be awaited to get the eventual result of
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1066]: func
                - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1067]: "This coroutine function is primarily intended to be used for executing IO-bound functions/methods that would otherwise block the event loop if they were run in the main thread. For example:"
              - generic [ref=f83e1068]: "def blocking_io(): print(f\"start blocking_io at {time.strftime('%X')}\") # Note that time.sleep() can be replaced with any blocking # IO-bound operation, such as file operations. time.sleep(1) print(f\"blocking_io complete at {time.strftime('%X')}\") async def main(): print(f\"started main at {time.strftime('%X')}\") await asyncio.gather( asyncio.to_thread(blocking_io), asyncio.sleep(1)) print(f\"finished main at {time.strftime('%X')}\") asyncio.run(main()) # Expected output: # # started main at 19:50:53 # start blocking_io at 19:50:53 # blocking_io complete at 19:50:54 # finished main at 19:50:54"
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1071]:
                - text: Directly calling
                - code [ref=f83e1072]: blocking_io()
                - text: in any coroutine would block the event loop for its duration, resulting in an additional 1 second of run time. Instead, by using
                - code [ref=f83e1073]: asyncio.to_thread()
                - text: ", we can run it in a separate thread without blocking the event loop."
              - generic [ref=f83e1074]:
                - paragraph [ref=f83e1075]: "Note:"
                - paragraph [ref=f83e1076]:
                  - text: Due to the
                  - link "GIL" [ref=f83e1077] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: ../glossary.html#term-GIL
                  - text: ","
                  - code [ref=f83e1078]: asyncio.to_thread()
                  - text: can typically only be used to make IO-bound functions non-blocking. However, for extension modules that release the GIL or alternative Python implementations that don’t have one,
                  - code [ref=f83e1079]: asyncio.to_thread()
                  - text: can also be used for CPU-bound functions.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1081]: Added in version 3.9.
        - generic [ref=f83e1082]:
          - heading [level=2] [ref=f83e1083]:
            - link "Scheduling from other threads" [ref=f83e1084] [cursor=pointer]:

          - generic [ref=f83e1085]:
            - term [ref=f83e1086]:
              - generic [ref=f83e1087]: asyncio.
              - generic [ref=f83e1088]: run_coroutine_threadsafe
              - text: (
              - emphasis [ref=f83e1089]:

              - emphasis [ref=f83e1091]:

            - definition [ref=f83e1093]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1094]: Submit a coroutine to the given event loop. Thread-safe.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1095]:
                - text: Return a
                - link [ref=f83e1096] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: concurrent.futures.html#concurrent.futures.Future
                  - code [ref=f83e1097]: concurrent.futures.Future
                - text: to wait for the result from another OS thread.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1098]: "This function is meant to be called from a different OS thread than the one where the event loop is running. Example:"
              - generic [ref=f83e1099]: "def in_thread(loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop) -> None: # Run some blocking IO pathlib.Path(\"example.txt\").write_text(\"hello world\", encoding=\"utf8\") # Create a coroutine coro = asyncio.sleep(1, result=3) # Submit the coroutine to a given loop future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(coro, loop) # Wait for the result with an optional timeout argument assert future.result(timeout=2) == 3 async def amain() -> None: # Get the running loop loop = asyncio.get_running_loop() # Run something in a thread await asyncio.to_thread(in_thread, loop)"
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1102]: "It’s also possible to run the other way around. Example:"
              - generic [ref=f83e1103]: "@contextlib.contextmanager def loop_in_thread() -> Generator[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop]: loop_fut = concurrent.futures.Future[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop]() stop_event = asyncio.Event() async def main() -> None: loop_fut.set_result(asyncio.get_running_loop()) await stop_event.wait() with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(1) as tpe: complete_fut = tpe.submit(asyncio.run, main()) for fut in concurrent.futures.as_completed((loop_fut, complete_fut)): if fut is loop_fut: loop = loop_fut.result() try: yield loop finally: loop.call_soon_threadsafe(stop_event.set) else: fut.result() # Create a loop in another thread with loop_in_thread() as loop: # Create a coroutine coro = asyncio.sleep(1, result=3) # Submit the coroutine to a given loop future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(coro, loop) # Wait for the result with an optional timeout argument assert future.result(timeout=2) == 3"
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1106]: "If an exception is raised in the coroutine, the returned Future will be notified. It can also be used to cancel the task in the event loop:"
              - generic [ref=f83e1107]: "try: result = future.result(timeout) except TimeoutError: print('The coroutine took too long, cancelling the task...') future.cancel() except Exception as exc: print(f'The coroutine raised an exception: {exc!r}') else: print(f'The coroutine returned: {result!r}')"
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1110]:
                - text: See the
                - link "concurrency and multithreading" [ref=f83e1111] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-dev.html#asyncio-multithreading
                - text: section of the documentation.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1112]:
                - text: Unlike other asyncio functions this function requires the
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1113]: loop
                - text: argument to be passed explicitly.

            - definition [ref=f83e1200]:
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1201]:
                - text: A
                - link [ref=f83e1202] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-future.html#asyncio.Future
                  - code [ref=f83e1203]: Future-like
                - text: object that runs a Python
                - link "coroutine" [ref=f83e1204] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#coroutine"
                - text: . Not thread-safe.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1205]:
                - text: Tasks are used to run coroutines in event loops. If a coroutine awaits on a Future, the Task suspends the execution of the coroutine and waits for the completion of the Future. When the Future is
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1206]: done
                - text: ", the execution of the wrapped coroutine resumes."
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1207]: "Event loops use cooperative scheduling: an event loop runs one Task at a time. While a Task awaits for the completion of a Future, the event loop runs other Tasks, callbacks, or performs IO operations."
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1208]:
                - text: Use the high-level
                - link [ref=f83e1209] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.create_task"
                  - code [ref=f83e1210]: asyncio.create_task()
                - text: function to create Tasks, or the low-level
                - link [ref=f83e1211] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-eventloop.html#asyncio.loop.create_task
                  - code [ref=f83e1212]: loop.create_task()
                - text: or
                - link [ref=f83e1213] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-future.html#asyncio.ensure_future
                  - code [ref=f83e1214]: ensure_future()
                - text: functions. Manual instantiation of Tasks is discouraged.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1215]:
                - text: To cancel a running Task use the
                - link [ref=f83e1216] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.Task.cancel"
                  - code [ref=f83e1217]: cancel()
                - text: method. Calling it will cause the Task to throw a
                - link [ref=f83e1218] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
                  - code [ref=f83e1219]: CancelledError
                - text: exception into the wrapped coroutine. If a coroutine is awaiting on a future-like object during cancellation, the awaited object will be cancelled.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1220]:
                - link [ref=f83e1221] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.Task.cancelled"
                  - code [ref=f83e1222]: cancelled()
                - text: can be used to check if the Task was cancelled. The method returns
                - code [ref=f83e1223]: "True"
                - text: if the wrapped coroutine did not suppress the
                - link [ref=f83e1224] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.CancelledError
                  - code [ref=f83e1225]: CancelledError
                - text: exception and was actually cancelled.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1226]:
                - link [ref=f83e1227] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.Task"
                  - code [ref=f83e1228]: asyncio.Task
                - text: inherits from
                - link [ref=f83e1229] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-future.html#asyncio.Future
                  - code [ref=f83e1230]: Future
                - text: all of its APIs except
                - link [ref=f83e1231] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-future.html#asyncio.Future.set_result
                  - code [ref=f83e1232]: Future.set_result()
                - text: and
                - link [ref=f83e1233] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: asyncio-future.html#asyncio.Future.set_exception
                  - code [ref=f83e1234]: Future.set_exception()
                - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1235]:
                - text: An optional keyword-only
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1236]: context
                - text: argument allows specifying a custom
                - link [ref=f83e1237] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: contextvars.html#contextvars.Context
                  - code [ref=f83e1238]: contextvars.Context
                - text: for the
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1239]: coro
                - text: to run in. If no
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1240]: context
                - text: is provided, the Task copies the current context and later runs its coroutine in the copied context.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1241]:
                - text: An optional keyword-only
                - emphasis [ref=f83e1242]: eager_start
                - text: argument allows eagerly starting the execution of the
                - link [ref=f83e1243] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#asyncio.Task"
                  - code [ref=f83e1244]: asyncio.Task
                - text: at task creation time. If set to
                - code [ref=f83e1245]: "True"
                - text: and the event loop is running, the task will start executing the coroutine immediately, until the first time the coroutine blocks. If the coroutine returns or raises without blocking, the task will be finished eagerly and will skip scheduling to the event loop.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1246]:
                - text: Tasks are
                - link "generic" [ref=f83e1247] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: typing.html#generics
                - text: over the return type of their wrapped coroutines.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1249]:
                - text: "Changed in version 3.7: Added support for the"
                - link [ref=f83e1250] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: contextvars.html#module-contextvars
                  - code [ref=f83e1251]: contextvars
                - text: module.
              - paragraph [ref=f83e1253]:
                - text: "Changed in version 3.8: Added the"

              - generic [ref=f83e1264]:
                - term [ref=f83e1265]:
                  - generic [ref=f83e1266]: done
                  - text: ()
                - definition [ref=f83e1267]:
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e1268]:
                    - text: Return
                    - code [ref=f83e1269]: "True"
                    - text: if the Task is
                    - emphasis [ref=f83e1270]: done
                    - text: .
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e1271]:
                    - text: A Task is
                    - emphasis [ref=f83e1272]: done
                    - text: when the wrapped coroutine either returned a value, raised an exception, or the Task was cancelled.
              - generic [ref=f83e1273]:
                - term [ref=f83e1274]:
                  - generic [ref=f83e1275]: result
                  - text: ()
                - definition [ref=f83e1276]:
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e1277]: Return the result of the Task.
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e1278]:
                    - text: If the Task is
                    - emphasis [ref=f83e1279]: done
                    - text: ", the result of the wrapped coroutine is returned (or if the coroutine raised an exception, that exception is re-raised.)"
                  - paragraph [ref=f83e1280]:
                    - text: If the Task has been
                    - emphasis [ref=f83e1281]: cancelled
